cards.explanation: The answer is True, friends. God says, "I dispersed them among the nations, and they were scattered throughout the lands." He adds, "I judged them according to their ways and deeds." I think this one hurts.

The answer is that they are the LORD's people yet had to leave His land, friends. Wherever they went, it was said of them, "These are the people of the LORD, yet they had to leave His land." God says that wherever they went, they profaned His holy name. I think that's a lot to carry around, being the walking headline.

The answer is False, friends. God tells the house of Israel, "It is not for your sake that I will act, O house of Israel, but for My holy name, which you profaned among the nations to which you went." So the reason He gives is His holy name. I'd say that's a message worth reading twice.

The answer is that the nations will know He is the LORD, friends. God says, "Then the nations will know that I am the LORD, declares the Lord GOD…" He says this will happen when He shows His holiness in Israel before their eyes. The knowing is about Him, not about anybody else.

The answer is Israel, friends. God says He'll show His holiness "…in you before their eyes." and He's speaking to the house of Israel. So the nations will watch it happen in the very people who profaned His name. That's a front row seat.

The answer is False, friends. God says, "I will also sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean. I will cleanse you from all your impurities and all your idols." Count the "I wills." God is the one doing the cleaning.

The answer is idols, friends. God says, "I will cleanse you from all your impurities and all your idols." Earlier He said they defiled the land with their idols (Ezekiel 36:18). So this cleansing reaches the very thing He named back then.

The answer is a heart of stone for a heart of flesh, friends. God says, "I will remove your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh." Stone is hard, and flesh is the living kind of heart. And notice it's God who removes the one and gives the other.

The answer is that He'll cause them to walk in His laws and keep them carefully, friends. God says, "And I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My statutes and to carefully observe My ordinances." Look at how it starts: He puts His Spirit within them first. Then the walking follows.

The answer is True, friends. God says, "you will be My people, and I will be your God." Those words come right after He says they'll live in the land He gave their forefathers. It's a simple line, and it says a lot.

The answer is mocked, friends. The verse says Israel will "…no longer bear reproach among the nations on account of famine." Reproach is the shame others pile on you. So God's plentiful crops lift that off them.

The answer is hate, friends. God says, "Then you will remember your evil ways and wicked deeds, and you will loathe yourselves for your iniquities and abominations." Loathe is a strong word, and it's the one God uses. Hate fits, because it's how they will feel about themselves.

The answer is ashamed and disgraced for their ways, friends. God says, "Be ashamed and disgraced for your ways, O house of Israel!" It comes right after "It is not for your sake that I will act…" I think this is a heavy verse.

The answer is True, friends. God says, "On the day I cleanse you from all your iniquities, I will cause the cities to be resettled and the ruins to be rebuilt." He ties the two together: the cleansing and the rebuilding. And He's the one saying "…I will cause…"

The answer is Eden, friends. The people will say, "This land that was desolate has become like the garden of Eden." Genesis 2:8 says God planted a garden in Eden, in the east. So the desolate land is going to be compared to that garden.
The answer is their plea, friends. God says, "Once again I will hear the plea of the house of Israel…" A plea is a request made to Him. And "once again" tells me they've been heard by Him before.

The answer is flocks for sacrifices, friends. God says, "Like the numerous flocks for sacrifices at Jerusalem during her appointed feasts, so the ruined cities will be filled with flocks of people." At the feasts those flocks were many, and that's the picture He picks. That's a lot of people.
